name: DBMaker
tagline: SYSCOM's ODBC-native SQL database from Taiwan, known for letting COBOL programs use SQL tables.
description: DBMaker is a commercial relational database developed by Taiwan's SYSCOM Group since the mid-1990s and still actively released: version 5.4.8 arrived in July 2026, adding AES network encryption and per-user connection limits. Its ODBC interface is native rather than a translation layer, it ships JDBC drivers, and it supports SQL stored procedures, triggers, large-object and file-object storage, online backup and crash recovery. The feature that keeps it relevant is DCI, a COBOL interface that maps AcuCOBOL, isCOBOL and Micro Focus file I/O (READ, WRITE, REWRITE, DELETE) straight onto database tables, so legacy indexed-file COBOL applications can move to SQL without rewriting their data access. Outside Taiwan and its partner network it is rarely seen.

pricing.notes: Commercial licences through SYSCOM and partners; a 90-day evaluation edition is downloadable.

scale.notes: Single-server engine scaled vertically; aimed at departmental and ISV-embedded deployments.

strengths: DCI lets AcuCOBOL, isCOBOL and Micro Focus programs keep their file-I/O verbs while data lives in SQL tables
ODBC is the native call interface, so ODBC tools connect without an extra translation layer
Stores multimedia as BLOBs or as database-managed external file objects
Steady release cadence: 5.4.7 in June 2025 and 5.4.8 in July 2026
weaknesses: Tiny footprint outside Taiwan; English documentation and community help are thin
No clustering, sharding or managed cloud offering
Proprietary licensing with prices only via sales
useCases: Migrating legacy COBOL indexed-file applications to a relational store
ISV-bundled databases for Taiwanese enterprise and government software
Departmental OLTP on Windows or Linux servers
notIdealFor: Teams needing a large global talent pool or ecosystem
